      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya</link>
      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/23/russia-ukraine-war-zelenskyy-libya-benghazi-drone-attack-ship-merkury-un-nato-europe-latest-news-updates">Europe live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:07:45 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Perspective</category><title>Photographer Federico Veronesi: 'I've been in love with African wildlife since I was three'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261123-photographer-federico-veronesi-i-ve-been-in-love-with-african-wildlife-since-i-was-three</link><description>
The winner of this year's Wildlife Photographer of the Year award has told FRANCE 24 that his winning picture reveals a lot about the complexity of an elephant's soul and feelings. At first glance the image seems to show a mother elephant playing with her calf, but in fact it is a female carrying another elephant's dead calf. Photographer Federico Veronesi told us how he fell in love in Kenya as a six-year-old child and ended up moving there to fulfil his photography dream. He spoke to us in Perspective.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b43bbd64-e736-11f1-ab72-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-9abe55f6.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b43bbd64-e736-11f1-ab72-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-9abe55f6.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fea82430-e729-11f1-a255-ffa9643d4a47</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 12:18:13 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Stuart NORVAL</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>'Out of control': ICE agents make arrests at Seattle airport in 'horrific' scene</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261123-out-of-control-ice-agents-make-arrests-at-seattle-airport-in-horrific-scene</link><description>
The governor of Washington state called US federal immigration agents "out of control" after they arrested two people at Seattle's main airport on Saturday. ICE officers have conducted raids across the United States, part of President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown which has forged ahead despite a rebuke by voters at this month's midterms.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ I’m planning my first dark sky trip, and all because this educational star projector showed me what I’m missing ]]> I didn’t expect much as I unboxed the Brainstorm Night Sky; after all, I’m significantly older than this educational star projector’s target audience. Perhaps I’d come away with a sense of wonder and delight, coupled with mild irritation at having to hunt down three AA batteries to power it.

Instead, I was filled with envy as the Brainstorm Night Sky reminded me just what I was missing, thanks to the rigors of light pollution. A few minutes after powering it down, I was already making plans for my first dark sky trip, yearning for a view that rivaled the Brainstorm’s cosmic images.

Brainstorm Night Sky Projector review

Whatever your age, the Brainstorm Night Sky is so simple to use

Draw the curtains, press the Night Sky’s single button (tilting the projector and twisting the focus as appropriate) and it projects a circular image onto a ceiling or wall. Press the button again and the projection slowly begins to rotate, slowly but stutter-free. It really is that simple to operate and, aimed at budding astronomers aged eight or above, it's reasonably lightweight without feeling flimsy.

Specifications

Weight: 14.8 oz (420 g)
Bulb type: Non-specified
Laser: No
Control: On-unit
Rotation: Yes, one speed
Projection area: Up to 8.2 ft (2.5 m)
Sleep timer: Yes (30 mins)
Power: 3x AA batteries
Speaker: No

I was initially a little surprised by the size of the projection: at up to 8.2 feet (2.5 m) wide it’s not going to fill an entire ceiling. It also switches off after 30 minutes, a limit that can’t be disabled, so if you’re looking to put on your own space-themed party this is not the projector for you. But it’s on point for home education and, priced from $49.99, the Brainstorm Night Sky projector won’t break the bank.

There’s minimal distortion around the edge of the images; the planets are spherical from the word go, unlike some projectors where I’ve had to tweak them to stop Mars turning into an egg. And I never once had to crane my neck because half the solar system had been projected onto a bookcase.

This projector revealed what light pollution had taken from me

The Brainstorm Night Sky model I tested comes with four slides, each with a case to protect them from smudges and sticky fingers. You place one into the provided slide housing then insert that into the projector. There’s the moon, the solar system, and two showing the Northern Hemisphere’s night sky, as seen from Hawaii (a key location for astronomy).

I can appreciate the educational value of the first couple, even if I am still seething at Pluto being demoted back in 2006. But it was the latter pair of slides that really opened my eyes to what I could be seeing over my head.

I can spot maybe 10-20 stars from my backyard, cloud cover permitting; thanks to light pollution, that’s it. Even though the best stargazing apps can show me what I should see, when I step outside, all I typically see with the naked eye is the odd pinprick in the void.

But as soon as I inserted that third slide, a striking stellar display appeared above my head, with more stars than I could hope to count. Even knowing that Hawaii’s night sky stretches far further than eight feet across, the difference between this view and the one from my house was like night and day. Brainstorm claims this slide features over 20,000 stars, though that’s likely referring to the source photo rather than the projected image.

The fourth slide — the same crisp starscape but with every visible constellation labelled — was almost as attention-grabbing. Educational value aside, it drove home that I couldn’t see the majority of these star patterns to name them, my local night sky is that polluted.

Knowing what I was missing out on made me determined to take my stargazing further afield. Some of the best smart telescopes can lessen the impact of light pollution, but stepping away from skyglow is the most effective option. Hawaii’s a little far to travel, but I’ve already started looking into local dark sky sites. I just need to grab a pair of the best binoculars for stargazing, hop on my bike and I’m ready to go.

The Brainstorm Night Sky is a solid, budget-priced educational tool, but it has one drawback

The Brainstorm Night Sky’s projections are crisp enough that you can easily make out every constellation name, but they could be a hair brighter. The Ainael Meter Galaxy Projector, for example, delivers more illumination.

If you want to use the Brainstorm Night Sky to relax, the rotate function gives its projections an oddly hypnotic effect, and the device is whisper-quiet to boot. And while Brainstorm doesn’t specify battery life, one set of rechargeables lasted me for several days.

Unfortunately, the Brainstorm Night Sky's slide collection is a little limited. There are two models, a blue version with four slides (the one I tested) and a gray version with six slides (featuring additional space shuttle and black hole images). The included instructions state you can purchase an additional slide disc showing the Southern Hemisphere’s stars, but that’s a maximum of seven images. Nor is this projector compatible with the slides from the Brainstorm Deep Sky Projector

It’s a little disappointing given that Brainstorm has clearly put thought into the projector’s educational value. Those instructions double as a poster of the solar system, and children can use a “secret code” (printed on the instructions) to explore more astronomy facts on the company’s website.

Offering extra slide packs, of the kind you can buy for the Pococo Galaxy Projector, would give it more long-term appeal. As is, I can see its novelty and educational value diminishing over time, at which point you can upgrade to one of the best star projectors.

If you’re not bothered by the lack of expandability, the Brainstorm Night Sky’s price, image quality and ease of use still make it a useful tool for kindling a child’s interest in astronomy, or as a budget-friendly gift for junior stargazers. It’s certainly spurred me into action — how much is a plane ticket to Hawaii, anyway?

]]> <![CDATA[ What did the Soviet Union's final deep space probe actually see on Mars? ]]> On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service.

However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been.

So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure?

Last of the Soviet space explorers

Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June.

To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising."

This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects.

A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity. This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across.

Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass.

Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly.

One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual.

SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass.

The spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters.

When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them.

The Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. "Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," said Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us."

The discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX launches 2 rockets from same pad 32 hours apart, smashing turnaround record (video) ]]>

SpaceX set a new record with its latest satellite launch out of California.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Launch Complex-4E on Sunday (Nov. 22) at 7:23 a.m. ET (1223 GMT; 4:23 a.m. local time in California), on a mission for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) called NROL-136.

It was the second launch from that pad in a little over 32 hours, after the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force. And that quick turnaround made history.

"Massive high five to the @SpaceX west coast team for a world record launch to launch turn from Pad 4e last night! 32 hr, 3 min, 21 sec! This smashed the previous record of 45 hrs from Pad 40. Team got there with several hours of margin. Next goal… the 24 hr turn!" Kiko Dontchev, SpaceX's vice president of launch, said via X on Sunday. (Pad 40 is at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.)

NROL-136 was the sixth launch of 2026 so far for the NRO. All of them have been carried out by SpaceX's workhorse Falcon 9, and all have delivered classified satellites to low Earth orbit.

The launch marked another step in the NRO's effort to expand its intelligence-gathering capabilities through a proliferated network of spacecraft designed to provide more frequent and timely surveillance of locations around the globe.

About two minutes after liftoff, the Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued carrying the classified payloads onward to orbit. The booster then reversed course and returned to Vandenberg, touching down at Landing Zone 4 approximately seven and a half minutes after launch.

Saturday's launch was the 14th flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster, dubbed B1097, which previously launched NASA's Sentinel-6B ocean-monitoring satellite, NROL-172, USSF-259 for the Space Force, and eight Starlink missions.

NROL-136 was the 15th launch dedicated to building the NRO's "proliferated architecture," the satellites for which have been developed in partnership with SpaceX and Northrop Grumman. The network is designed to increase coverage and improve the "capability and resilience" of U.S. intelligence operations in space, according to the NRO's mission website.

The NRO began deploying the constellation in May 2024 with the launch of NROL-146. The most recent proliferated architecture mission before Sunday was NROL-179, which lifted off on June 19, 2026.

As with any classified mission, the agency has not disclosed the exact number of satellites aboard NROL-136 or revealed details about their onboard technologies.

Editor's note: This story was updated at 11 p.m. ET on Nov. 22 with the news that NROL-136 set a new record for the shortest time between two launches from the same pad.

]]> <![CDATA[ This viral star projector has been hyped to Mars and back, but we hunted down the best version you can buy ]]> It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again.

I tempered my expectations when I first got my hands on the Galaxy Projector Night Light. Packed in a small, relatively unassuming box, it looks remarkably similar to the standard model that’s spread across TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and so on. Just like that one, it’s powered via USB, with a flexible stalk, a slot for slides and a nose-mounted focus wheel.

However, once I hooked it up to a handy USB socket, all my reservations vanished, and I was seriously impressed by the power of this little projector. You’ll need a darkened room but the Galaxy Projector Night Light’s larger lens is a serious step-up from the run-of-the-mill version. Its images are richer and clearer than you’d expect from a projector this size, and easily capable of transforming a mid-sized ceiling or wall into a cosmic display.

This stunning James Webb Space Telescope image of the Pillars of Creation, with its vast columns of gas and dust, is a perfect example of the projections on offer. The fact the display was static didn’t diminish its wow factor, and I spent a good 15 minutes gazing at it in wonder.

The Galaxy Projector Night Light does have a four-hour shut-off in case you drift off or want to use it to lull a child to sleep (and 12 hours for its night light function). It’s easy to adjust thanks to its flexible neck, and while it never once came loose, you’ll find some USB ports have a tighter grip than others.

Slide selection

Once I set aside the images of Santa Claus (you’re staying in the box, Saint Nick), jellyfish and a T. rex, I was left with 10 astronomy-related slides. Several, such as the black hole, are artistic illustrations, while others, like the aforementioned Pillars, are actual astronomical images.

They all have their own distinct appeal. I wouldn’t, for example, describe the black hole slide as relaxing, but it’s absolutely captivating in a cosmic horror way. I’d have appreciated an auto-rotate option, but that would have added some bulk to the projector.

Switching slides is a breeze, each image mounted in its own slide holder. Oddly, a couple of mine had hair-like marks, but those disappeared when I brought the image into focus via the nose wheel.

The full 13-slide set is:

• Angel and stars (B&W)
• Black hole
• Earth and moon
• Jellyfish
• Magellanic Cloud
• Milky Way
• Moon and stars (B&W)
• Pillars of Creation
• Santa
• Solar system
• Starfield (B&W)
• T. rex
• Whale and stars (B&W)

It’s mildly disappointing that there aren’t extra slide packs out there, but the selection is ample for entertainment, relaxation and even education. What better way to spark an interest in STEM than with the wonders of space?

Portable projection

The Galaxy Projector Night Light will run off any USB port: a laptop, desktop, charger and so on. I even got it working with my TV’s USB socket, but the real bonus was realizing I could run it off the best power banks. If you’re on the move, slip the projector and slides into one pocket, a powerbank into another, and you’re good to go for hours.

Some of the best star projectors are styled so they blend in with a room, but this one is so small you can just pack it away until you need it. The projector’s marketing even advertises it for use in the car, which seems like an accident waiting to happen. Only the Blisslights Starport is smaller, but then you’re limited to laser-dot stars.

There’s no remote and no sound options, but the Galaxy Projector Night Light is so easy to use that children should be able to get to grips with it. Literally, in fact, since while the light portion warms up, it never really gets hot. Factor in its small size and pocket-friendly price, and it’s an ideal space gift or stocking stuffer for a young stargazer.

As long as you don’t buy the hype and think you’re getting something that’ll bathe a room in beautifully animated starscapes, as several Amazon purchasers did, you’ll find this Galaxy Projector Night Light is a surprisingly capable little star projector.

Are there bigger and better models out there? Yes, and we’ve rounded up the best star projectors if this one isn’t for you. But for convenience, value for money and portability, this Galaxy Projector Night Light is a great way to bring the cosmos into your home and it’s fast cemented itself as one of my favorites.

]]> <![CDATA[ As 'Star Trek: First Contact' turns 30, Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview) ]]> "Star Trek: First Contact" celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart, last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance.

Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes, in his feature film debut, "First Contact" consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved.

Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism.

Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget.

Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"?

We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile!

"What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. ILM’s John Knoll, the guy who won the Oscar for 'Star Wars,' just happened to be our Special Effects Supervisor."

"First Contact" is filled with memorable moments and indelible performances, some of which certainly stand out for Frakes looking back over the years on the production.

"The two things that always come to mind were the beautiful scene with Alfre [Woodard] and Patrick, the Moby Dick scene, where she says, 'You broke your little ships,'" he recalls. "I was sitting under the camera with my face in my hands, watching two heavyweights go at it take after take. It was what you dream of. They were into it. The writing was great. We had time to do it right, and they were fabulous together.

"That and the Cromwell and Marina drunk on tequila scene. It's not only one extended take, but it contributes to the pace of the movie in the right kind of way. My wife tells me that I was really good in that scene because I was exhausted and relaxed. It’s true, you’re exhausted when you’re filming and acting at the same time. I got to sit there and watch those two. It was like watching a tennis game."

Many Trekkies might not know that Alfre Woodard is Frakes' godmother, and he had specifically asked producer Rick Berman for approval to include her in the movie’s cast.

"She's one of our finest American actors," he notes. "Rick said, 'If we can get Alfre, that would be great.' I knew she’d do great with Patrick, so that was a no-brainer. I never had a godmother, and when I came out here to live in LA back in 1979, an old friend from college, Nathan Cook, was working with Alfre. We were at a barbecue, and it came up. She said, 'You don’t have a godmother? I’ll be your godmother.' I asked what that meant, and she said, 'I’ll be in charge of your spiritual being.' It's been a magical friendship that turned into her playing that part."

The hive-minded cybernetic collective known as the Borg featured prominently in the time-travel tale, and that second filming unit did a masterful job lighting those scenes.

"The Borg costumes were torture, from what I was told," says Frakes. "We had our own set of ADs and an entirely separate special effects makeup crew, and the costume department had a certain number of Borg to build and rebuild. Now the Borg had been on the show, but with these Borg we had more time and more moving parts. It was kind of an enhanced thing that really paid off. I look back so fondly on that entire experience. Also, the Borg were one of the great movie villains. They held up!"

Frakes couldn’t be prouder of "First Contact", and he reminds us that most people like it right next to 1982's "Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan." That's rarefied air indeed!

"We got Cromwell coming off of 'Babe.' So we had Alfre and Alice and Cromwell. They joined our family effortlessly. Because we'd done seven TV seasons, 182 episodes, and a movie already together, we were thick as thieves and still are; may Patrick rest in peace. The three of them joined us as if we’d been dancing with them forever."

On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night.

This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites.

The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified.

Why it mattered

From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station.

The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs).

As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together.

]]> <![CDATA[ 10 things that worry me about chasing the 2027 total solar eclipse in Egypt ]]> On Aug. 2, 2027, I'll be in Luxor, Egypt, to witness what could be the greatest total solar eclipse of my life. However, clouds aren't the only thing that can obscure the sun. Dust and sand are potential hazards in the Egyptian desert, and a dust storm at the wrong moment could affect—though probably not ruin—the view. Although the sun will almost certainly be visible during the eclipse, airborne dust could hide the delicate structure of the solar corona.

2. Chaos in Luxor

How many people will descend on Luxor for the eclipse? August is normally a quiet month for tourism in Luxor because of the oppressive heat. In 2027, however, the city and its surrounding urban area — population about four million — could swell as eclipse chasers, tour groups, photographers and curious visitors descend. Hotels, roads, buses and archaeological sites will all face extraordinary pressure. Authorities there had a plan for its west coast, the prime viewing region. "They were going to start closing roads from 3 p.m. on the afternoon of the eclipse," said Simon Waldram, who runs astrophotography and landscape photography workshops and who drove his tour group to the intended viewing location at 8 o'clock on the morning of the eclipse. Luxor in August is brutally hot. Temperatures can exceed 104 degrees Fahrenheit (40 degrees Celsius). Totality will strike at 1:02 p.m. local time (EEST). Many tour groups will stay on their hotel grounds or remain on cruise ships — relatively close to shade and air-con — though I'm also planning to keep a wet towel around my neck and carry plenty of water. I'll be traveling on the Nile, which sounds like a wonderfully romantic way to experience an eclipse. However, there's speculation that river traffic could be restricted, perhaps even from the previous day. "There might be a restriction on navigation on the Nile during the eclipse, so it's a bit hard to plan where we are going to watch it," said ElSamman. Even if we're safely moored in Luxor, how many other vessels will be there? The Nile looks set to be packed with cruise ships, traditional dahabiyas and smaller boats, all carrying people hoping to witness the same extraordinary event. I wonder what totality will actually look and sound like. Will there be music? Shouting? Bright lights from neighboring boats? Probably — though perhaps that's no bad thing. Watching a total solar eclipse from Karnak or another ancient Egyptian temple sounds almost impossibly romantic. But the reality could be very different. Every eclipse chaser who plans and books a hotel years in advance dreads the email that often arrives a few weeks before, saying a reservation has been canceled for some spurious reason. This has already happened in Luxor, where prices have already reached about $600 per person per night for the week of the eclipse — roughly seven times higher than usual. I've witnessed totality on a tennis court at sunset, standing next to a horse on a mountain and on a cruise ship in the Southern Ocean — among others — but I've never encountered the eclipsed sun almost directly overhead. Six minutes is a long time to stare almost vertically upward. Finding a comfortable position could make a surprisingly big difference to how much I enjoy the spectacle.

To spend six uninterrupted minutes studying the sun's ghostly corona, watching its delicate streamers stretch into space, is almost beyond comprehension.  <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/na-ceskobudejovickem-sidlisti-otevreli-setkavarnu-komunitni-prostor-obsluhuji_2611231145_raf</link>
 <description>Nezisková organizace Aditus Pro otevřela na českobudějovickém sídlišti Vltava kavárnu s názvem Setkávárna. Část jejích zaměstnanců tvoří lidé se zdravotním postižením, kteří mají jinak problém s pracovním začleněním. Kavárna bude sloužit také jako komunitní prostor. „Moc doufáme, že si sem lidé ze sídliště najdou cestu a že sem budou chodit rádi a často,“ říká pro Český rozhlas České Budějovice ředitel organizace Aditus Pro Jan Šesták.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Policie navrhla obžalovat psychoterapeuta z Prahy, který měl zneužívat ženy. Hrozí mu až 10 let vězení</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/policie-navrhla-obzalovat-psychoterapeuta-z-prahy-ktery-mel-zneuzivat-zeny-hrozi_2611231149_vdv</link>
 <description>Pražští kriminalisté navrhli obžalovat 53letého psychoterapeuta, který dle nich zneužíval a znásilňoval klientky. Muž měl pracoviště na Hradčanech, kde převážně přes noc prováděl terapie. Ženám při nich údajně podával drogy a pak využil jejich bezbrannosti. Policisté ho viní ze znásilnění, sexuálního útoku, útisku a nedovolené výroby a jiného nakládání s omamnými a psychotropními látkami a s jedy. Obvinění potvrdil mluvčí policie Richard Hrdina.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Muž z Valdic, který se pokusil zabít spoluvězně, dostal doživotní trest. Rozhodl o tom krajský soud</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/muz-z-valdic-ktery-se-pokusil-zabit-spoluvezne-dostal-dozivotni-trest-rozhodl-o_2611231136_zko</link>
 <description>Krajský soud v Hradci Králové odsoudil k doživotnímu trestu muže, který loni v listopadu ve Věznici Valdice na Jičínsku na cele zaútočil na spoluvězně. Napadený přežil. Soud obžalovaného potrestal za pokus o vraždu, informovali v pondělí zástupci krajského soudu. Muž, který si odpykává trest za násilné zločiny z let 2010 a 2015 v celkové délce trvání 30 let, se k činu doznal. Rozsudek zatím není pravomocný.</description>

   <description>Dnes již bývalý soudce Pravoslav Polák působil u Krajského soudu v Plzni pětatřicet let a za tu dobu soudil řadu závažných kauz. <title>Z další známé značky v české e-commerce unikla data zákazníků, útok zasáhl Dedoles</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/z-dalsi-zname-znacky-ceske-e-commerce-unikla-data-zakazniku-utok-zasahl-dedoles/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Zákazníci e-shopu Dedoles se musí mít na pozoru před podvodnými e-maily, SMS a telefonáty. E-shop zákazníkům oznámil, že při kybernetickém útoku na jeho dodavatele, slovenskou marketingovou a digitální agenturu ui42, získala neoprávněná osoba kopii dat ze star&#353;ího systému internetového obchodu Dedoles. Uniknout mohly osobní údaje zákazníků včetně jmen, adres, telefonních čísel, e-mailů a podrobností o jejich nákupech. Incident oznámila i společnost ui42.</description>

 <title>,Největší technologická jednotka protivníka.‘ Kde se vzal Rubikon, ruská elitní dronová skupina</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/rusko-rubikon-jednotka-drony_2611231100_ula</link>
 <description>Příslušníci dronové jednotky, či spíše „skupiny operátorů dronů, instruktorů a výzkumníků“ mají patřit mezi elitní části ruské armády. Jejich úkolem je ničit a eliminovat ukrajinské dronové kapacity. Podle některých Ukrajinců ale členové Rubikonu neváhají útočit na cokoli a chybí jim jakékoli zábrany. Podobně se pro ukrajinská média vyjadřoval rovněž jeden z jeho příslušníků, který se z jednotky rozhodl dezertovat a vzdát se ukrajinské straně.</description>

 <description>Ukrajinská bezposádková plavidla zasáhla u břehů severoafrické Libye dvě ruské lodě, uvedl v pondělí ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj. O explozi na palubě ruské korvety Merkurij informovala média v neděli. Podle Zelenského se jedna z nejnovějších ruských vojenských lodí potopila. Druhým cílem bylo nákladní plavidlo Angara, které nepřítel využíval k přepravě zbraní, napsal na sociální síti X Zelenskyj.</description>

 <description>Jak europoslanci vysvětlují voličům svoji práci? Jak pracují se sociálními sítěmi a připravují se na rozhovory? O tom v debatě Bruselských chlebíčků mluví pět europoslanců napříč politickým spektrem. „Součástí naší práce musí být i propagace – nejen své práce, ale i Evropy, kterou zastupujeme. Protože podívejme se na volební účast. To je naše vizitka,“ říká Markéta Gregorová z Pirátské strany. Alexandr Vondra z ODS jí ale oponuje.</description>

 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-po-utoku-dronu-hori-rafinerie-na-jihozapade-ruska-zare-na-obloze-je-videt_2611230724_lbl</link>
 <description>V petrochemickém závodu v Novošachtinsku na jihozápadě Ruska vypukl po tříhodinovém náletu ukrajinských dronů rozsáhlý požár. Podle očitých svědků hoří jedna ze skladovacích nádrží. Jasná záře na obloze je vidět desítky kilometrů daleko, napsal ruský server Kuzbass-segodnja. V Novošachtinsku podle portálu Donpress.ru hoří nejen rafinerie, ale i areál společnosti Tata-gaz, kde jsou sklady pohonných hmot. Ruské úřady se dosud nevyjádřily.</description>

 <description>Ukrajina musí ve svých reformách zrychlit, a to především pokud chce mít přístupová jednání hotová v roce 2028. Uvádí to nedávná zpráva Evropské komise hodnotící pokrok kandidátských zemí. „Kdyby se to zvládlo do konce přespříštího roku, bylo by to podle mě hodně optimistické,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iROZHLAS.cz politolog Petr Kaniok. Z pohledu Bruselu je podle něj navíc nepředstavitelné, aby se země k Evropské unii připojila, dokud je ve válce.</description>

 <description>V německém Rostocku kotví na řece Warnow více než 150 metrů dlouhá loď s poněkud nepatřičným názvem – Drážďany. Patří k prvním velkým nákladním lodím postaveným v bývalém východním Německu. Dnes už má své plavby za sebou a slouží jako muzeum lodního stavitelství a mořeplavby.  <description>Ruská záchranná loď začala v neděli z finských vod odtahovat poškozenou ruskou nákladní loď Sparta II, kterou v sobotu v Baltském moři zasáhly drony. Práce mají několikaměsíční zpoždění a město za úpravu okolí vodního díla zaplatí bezmála 90 milionů korun. Původně radnice počítala s částkou pod 80 milionů.</description></item><item><title>Poděkování fanouškům, absolutorium hráčům. Trenér Fodrek byl po Spartě spokojený</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906461-podekovani-fanouskum-absolutorium-hracum-trener-fodrek-byl-po-sparte-spokojeny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906461-podekovani-fanouskum-absolutorium-hracum-trener-fodrek-byl-po-sparte-spokojeny.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Ani po výhře 3:1 na Spartě u trenéra Slovanu Branislava Fodreka nebyl vidět úsměv. Sám ale mluvil o tom, že jeho tým na podzim čekají ještě čtyři další těžké zápasy.</description></item><item><title>V Libereckém kraji nasněžilo, silničáři radí opatrnost</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906448-v-libereckem-kraji-nasnezilo-a-misty-stale-snezi-silnicari-radi-opatrnost.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906448-v-libereckem-kraji-nasnezilo-a-misty-stale-snezi-silnicari-radi-opatrnost.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:33:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V Libereckém kraji do rána nasněžilo a místy se stále objevují sněhové přeháňky, silnice jsou s opatrností sjízdné. Na pomoc zvířeti, které tam s největší pravděpodobností někdo úmyslně odložil, zavolala kolemjdoucí žena strážníky. Kočičí holčička Bambi nyní bojuje se zdravotními potížemi v útulku.</description></item><item><title>Sparta ve výročním zápase překvapivě prohrála s Libercem 1:3</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906433-sparta-ve-vyrocnim-zapase-prekvapive-prohrala-s-libercem-1-3.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/906433-sparta-ve-vyrocnim-zapase-prekvapive-prohrala-s-libercem-1-3.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:09:16 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Fotbalisté Sparty v 15. kole první ligy ve výročním zápase překvapivě prohráli doma s Libercem 1:3 a v neúplné tabulce na čtvrté příčce ztrácejí na druhý Slovan již pět bodů. Severočeši zaostávají za vedoucí Slavií o osm bodů a k dobru mají dohrávaný duel s Ostravou.</description></item><item><title>Liberec čtyřmi góly ve druhé třetině otočil duel s Mladou Boleslaví a vyhrál 5:2</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906431-liberec-ctyrmi-goly-ve-druhe-tretine-otocil-duel-s-mladou-boleslavi-a-vyhral-5-2.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906431-liberec-ctyrmi-goly-ve-druhe-tretine-otocil-duel-s-mladou-boleslavi-a-vyhral-5-2.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Hokejisté Liberce porazili ve 21. kole extraligy na svém ledě Mladou Boleslav 5:2. Před svými diváky uspěli Bílí Tygři posedmé za sebou, derby ovládli počtvrté v řadě. Bruslaři si připsali pátou prohru z posledních šesti startů, přestože po první třetině vedli.</description></item><item><title>České domácnosti dluží přes 4,5 bilionu, spotřebitelský dluh roste rekordním tempem</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906313-ceske-domacnosti-dluzi-pres-4-5-bilionu-spotrebitelsky-dluh-roste-rekordnim-tempem.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906313-ceske-domacnosti-dluzi-pres-4-5-bilionu-spotrebitelsky-dluh-roste-rekordnim-tempem.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Miroslav Adamec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Podle údajů společnosti Czech Banking Credit Bureau (CBCB) dosáhlo celkové zadlužení obyvatel České republiky evidované v Bankovním a Nebankovním registru klientských informací na konci třetího čtvrtletí 2026 výše 4,53 bilionu korun.</description></item><item><title>Nová poznávací trasa připomene příběhy šesti zajímavých míst</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906306-nova-poznavaci-trasa-pripomene-pribehy-sesti-zajimavych-mist.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zpravy/906306-nova-poznavaci-trasa-pripomene-pribehy-sesti-zajimavych-mist.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 12:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Zuzana Pešková</dc:creator><category>Zprávy</category><description>Od kapličky přes hřbitov až k lesnímu divadlu. Stála něco málo přes 400 tisíc korun a slavnostně se otevře 6. prosince.</description></item><item><title>Odešla hokejová legenda.
